mainTopic: The end of a teaching about גיהנום, the 'בבלים' in the משנה, the timing of the לחם הפנים on the שולחן, and whether כלי שרת make things holy at the wrong time.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching about גיהנום. Each 'lest you say' raises a wrong idea, and a פסוק corrects it, ending with the promise that the righteous get real blessing, not just rescue. The גמרא then explains that the 'בבלים' in the משנה who ate the שעיר raw were really Alexandrians, called 'בבלים' as an insult, and רבי יהודה is relieved. A new משנה teaches that the לחם הפנים and בזיכין must sit on the שולחן a full week, from שבת to שבת, and that leaving them longer does no harm. The גמרא then quotes a משנה in יומא about checking for dawn before slaughtering the תמיד, because a תמיד slaughtered at night once had to be burned. אבוה דרבי אבין adds that a bird עולה pinched at night or a מנחה whose קומץ was taken at night is also burned, because כלי שרת make their contents holy even at the wrong time. The גמרא refines this: at the wrong time the כלי makes something holy enough to be disqualified, but not holy enough to be offered. רבי זירא challenges this from the bread placed after שבת, and רבה answers that a night early is not 'too early,' but days early is. The amud ends as the גמרא begins one more challenge, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: גיהנום is narrow at the opening but wide inside
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה finishes its earlier line and then answers a wrong idea: that גיהנום is narrow all the way through. The פסוק 'deep and wide' shows that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...within it. And in case you think that just as its opening is narrow, all of it is narrow, the פסוק says: 'deep and wide.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a line from the previous page about גיהנום. It then uses a פסוק from ישעיהו to reject the idea that גיהנום is narrow throughout.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The narrow opening was mentioned earlier. Someone might think the whole place is equally small. The words הֶעֱמִיק הִרְחִב teach that inside it is deep and wide.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mouth, meaning its opening
The פסוק teaches us
Made deep, made wide

phrases.english: within it.
phrases.notes: This word finishes a sentence from the previous page about גיהנום and its narrow opening.

phrases.english: And lest you say
just as its opening is narrow,
so all of it is narrow,
the verse states: 'deep and wide.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:33

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אגדה about גיהנום from the previous page.
steps.raayaObject: That גיהנום is wide inside, even though its opening is narrow

steps.title: גיהנום is prepared even for a king
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think important people like kings are not sent to גיהנום. The פסוק says it was prepared even for the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you think it was not prepared for a king, the פסוק says: 'It too is prepared for the king.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second wrong idea and corrects it with the same פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that no one is too important to be judged. Even a king is included.

keyTerms.meaning: It was prepared
It too is prepared for the king

phrases.english: And lest you say
it was not prepared for a king,
the verse states: 'It too is prepared for the king.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same chain of 'lest you say' lines.
steps.raayaObject: That גיהנום applies even to a king

steps.title: גיהנום has much wood for its fire
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think there is no wood in גיהנום. The פסוק says its pile is fire and much wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you think there is no wood in it, the פסוק says: 'Its pile is fire and much wood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third wrong idea and corrects it with the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the point is that the fire of גיהנום is fully fueled, not weak. The דרשה keeps moving word by word through ישעיהו 30:33.

keyTerms.meaning: Its pile, meaning its pile of fuel
Wood

phrases.english: And lest you say
there is no wood in it,
the verse states: 'Its pile is fire and much wood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the same chain.
steps.raayaObject: That גיהנום has plenty of fuel

steps.title: Escaping גיהנום is not the whole reward
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think that being saved from גיהנום is the only reward. A פסוק in איוב shows there is also a full table of blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you think this is the whole reward, the פסוק says: 'And what is set on your table is full of richness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the chain of teachings. It shows that the reward is more than just being rescued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier lines described how serious גיהנום is. This last line turns positive: the one who follows the right path is not only saved but also receives plenty and peace.

keyTerms.meaning: Its reward
What is set on your table
Fatness, meaning richness and plenty

steps.whatToRemember: The אגדה ends on a positive note. Escaping גיהנום is not the whole reward, because there is also real blessing.

phrases.english: And lest you say
this is its reward,
phrases.notes: He means: being saved from גיהנום is the only reward.

phrases.english: the verse states:
'And what is set on your table is full of fatness.'
phrases.notes: איוב 36:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item, which closes the chain of the אגדה.
steps.raayaObject: That the reward includes blessing, not only rescue

steps.title: Back to the משנה: יום הכפורים on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה about יום הכפורים falling on שבת, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יום הכפורים falls on שבת, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its opening words, getting ready to explain a detail in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'and so on' points to the rest of the משנה. That is where it says the 'בבלים' ate the goat offering raw when יום הכפורים fell on Friday. The next step explains who these people were.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement
And so on: the rest of the quote

phrases.english: If Yom Kippur occurs
on Shabbat, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, where the בבלים eat the שעיר raw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה as a heading for the coming discussion.

steps.title: The 'Babylonians' were really Alexandrians
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the כהנים who ate the meat raw were from Alexandria. They were called 'בבלים' only because people disliked the בבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They were not really from בבל. They were from Alexandria. But because people hated the בבלים, they called them by that name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains who the 'בבלים' in the משנה actually were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to blame people from בבל for eating raw meat in a crude way. רבי יוחנן says the real eaters were from Alexandria. The name 'בבלים' was used as an insult, because people in ארץ ישראל disliked the בבלים.

keyTerms.meaning: People from בבל
People from Alexandria in Egypt
They hate
By the name of

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as saying people from בבל really did this. רבי יוחנן says it was a nickname used as an insult.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They are not Babylonians,
rather they are Alexandrians,
and since they hate the Babylonians,
they call them by the name 'Babylonians.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'בבלים' in the משנה were really Alexandrians, called 'בבלים' as an insult.

steps.title: A ברייתא from רבי יוסי says the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying the same words as רבי יוחנן, which supports his explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי יוסי says, They were not from בבל but from Alexandria. Because people hated the בבלים, they called them by that name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's explanation is not new. An earlier תנא, רבי יוסי, already said the same thing, almost word for word.

keyTerms.meaning: Also like this: a sign that a source supports what was just said

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
Rabbi Yosei says:
They are not Babylonians,
rather they are Alexandrians,
and since they hate the Babylonians,
they call them by the name 'Babylonians.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the 'בבלים' were Alexandrians

steps.title: רבי יהודה is relieved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה thanks רבי יוסי: 'May your mind be at ease, because you put my mind at ease.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: May your mind rest, because you have put my mind at rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה reacts to רבי יוסי's explanation with thanks and relief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה was bothered by the משנה seeming to describe בבלים as crude eaters. רבי יוסי's explanation clears their name, and that puts רבי יהודה at ease.

keyTerms.meaning: May your mind be at rest: a blessing of thanks
You put my mind at rest

steps.whatToRemember: The 'בבלים' of the משנה were really Alexandrians. רבי יוחנן and רבי יוסי both say so, and רבי יהודה welcomes this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
May your mind be at ease,
for you have put my mind at ease.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה תָּנוּחַ דַּעְתְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה's reaction to רבי יוסי's statement in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explanation is accepted: the 'בבלים' were really Alexandrians, so the בבלים are cleared of the insult.

steps.title: Bread placed on שבת, bowls placed after שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the bread was set on the שולחן on שבת but the בזיכין only after שבת, and the לבונה was burned the next שבת, the bread is unfit. There is no liability for פיגול, נותר or טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone arranged the bread on שבת and the bowls after שבת, and then burned the bowls' frankincense on the next שבת, it is invalid. People are not liable for eating it because of פיגול, נותר or טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה gives its first case: the bread was put on the table at the right time, but the bowls of לבונה were put on late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בזיכין must sit on the שולחן for a full week, from שבת to שבת. Here they were only there for less than a week, so burning their לבונה does not make the bread permitted. These three prohibitions only apply to bread that was properly permitted, so none of them apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Arranged, set out on the שולחן
The two bowls of לבונה placed beside the לחם הפנים
Burned on the מזבח
A קרבן made unfit by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Leftover sacrificial food eaten after its time

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'not liable' here does not mean the bread may be eaten. The bread is פסול. The משנה is saying the specific punishments of פיגול, נותר and טמא do not apply, because the bread was never properly permitted in the first place.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one arranged the bread on Shabbat,
but the bowls only after Shabbat,
and he burned the bowls on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This means the following שבת, so the bowls were there for less than a full week.

phrases.english: it is invalid, and one is not liable for them
because of piggul, notar, or impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous section's discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the בזיכין were not on the שולחן for a full week, burning them does not permit the bread. The bread is unfit and is not subject to פיגול, נותר or טמא.

steps.title: Both placed on שבת, frankincense burned after the next שבת
steps.stepSummary: If both the bread and the bowls were set out on שבת, but the לבונה was burned after the next שבת, the bread is unfit. Again there is no liability for פיגול, נותר or טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone arranged the bread and the bowls on שבת, and burned the bowls' frankincense after שבת, it is invalid. People are not liable for it because of פיגול, נותר or טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. This time the placing was done right, but the burning happened too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is not that the time was too short. The problem is that the burning missed its proper time on שבת. Since the burning is invalid, the bread is never permitted, so the same three liabilities do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: After שבת, meaning after the proper time of burning on שבת had passed
Invalid, unfit
Here: eating holy food while ritually impure

phrases.aramaic: סִידֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶת הַבָּזִיכִין בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: If one arranged the bread and the bowls on Shabbat,
and burned the bowls after Shabbat,
it is invalid, and one is not liable for them
because of piggul, notar, or impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִידֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶת הַבָּזִיכִין בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה, with the mistake moved from the placing to the burning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the לבונה after its proper שבת is invalid. The bread is unfit and is not subject to פיגול, נותר or טמא.

steps.title: Both placed after שבת, and how to fix it
steps.stepSummary: If both were placed after שבת and burned on the next שבת, it is invalid. The fix is to leave them on the שולחן until the following שבת, since staying extra days does no harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone arranged the bread and the bowls after שבת and burned the bowls on the next שבת, it is invalid. What should he do? He should leave it for the following שבת, because even if it sits on the table for many days, that does no harm.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case and then teaches a practical solution so the bread does not become unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here everything was placed late, so by the next שבת nothing has been there a full week. Instead of removing it then, one waits one more שבת. This works because the only requirement is a minimum of one full week, and staying longer is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act?
He should leave it in place
The golden table in the היכל holding the לחם הפנים
There is nothing wrong with that

steps.whatToRemember: The לחם הפנים and בזיכין need a full week on the שולחן, from שבת to שבת, and the לבונה is burned on שבת. Too short a time or the wrong day of burning makes the bread unfit. Too long a time does no harm.

phrases.aramaic: סִידֵּר אֶת הַלֶּחֶם וְאֶת הַבָּזִיכִין לְאַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: If one arranged the bread and the bowls after Shabbat,
and burned the bowls on Shabbat, it is invalid.
How should he act?
He should leave it until the following Shabbat,
phrases.notes: He skips the next שבת and removes it the שבת after that, so a full week has passed.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הִיא עַל הַשּׁוּלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים –
phrases.english: for even if it is on the Table many days,
there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third case, which closes the משנה with a practical solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If everything was placed late, one leaves it until the following שבת. Extra time on the שולחן does not make it unfit.

steps.title: Checking whether it is time to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת יומא. The appointed כהן sends someone to check whether morning has come, and the observer answers 'בַּרְקַאי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: the appointed one said to them, 'Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has come.' If it has come, the observer says: 'There is light.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a different משנה, from יום הכפורים in the בית המקדש. It is setting up a discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבנות may not be slaughtered at night, so someone had to confirm that day had begun before slaughtering the morning תמיד. The answer 'בַּרְקַאי' was the signal that enough light had appeared.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
The כהן appointed to oversee the service
The time when slaughtering is allowed, meaning daytime
The one sent to look
'There is light', the signal that dawn has come

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in יומא 28a, about the יום הכפורים service.

phrases.english: The appointed one said to them:
'Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has arrived.'
If it has arrived, the observer says: 'There is light.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins with an outside source to set up its discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not slaughter until daylight is confirmed, and the observer signals it with 'בַּרְקַאי'.

steps.title: מתתיא בן שמואל waits for more light
steps.stepSummary: מתתיא בן שמואל used a stronger test. He asked whether the whole eastern sky was lit as far as חברון, and the observer answered 'Yes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מתתיא בן שמואל says: 'Is the whole east lit up, as far as חברון?' And he says: 'Yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה brings a second view. מתתיא בן שמואל required more light before slaughtering, and he used a different question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view is satisfied with the first light, 'בַּרְקַאי'. מתתיא בן שמואל waited until the light spread across the eastern sky all the way to חברון. Here the appointed כהן asks the question, and the observer simply answers 'הֵן'.

keyTerms.meaning: Has become light
The east, where the sun rises
A city south of ירושלים, used here as a landmark
Yes

phrases.english: Mattitya ben Shmuel says:
'Is the face of the entire east lit up
until the one at Hebron?'
phrases.notes: He means: has the light spread across the whole eastern sky, as far as חברון?

phrases.english: And he says: 'Yes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, stricter view within the same quoted משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to מתתיא בן שמואל, slaughtering waits until the whole eastern sky is lit as far as חברון.

steps.title: Why was the careful dawn check needed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why they needed to send someone to check for daylight so carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they need to do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks why the careful dawn check from steps 12 and 13 was set up. This question sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 described a detailed procedure for confirming morning. Now the משנה asks for the reason behind it, so the procedure won't look like extra strictness for no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: They needed to (do this)

phrases.english: And why did they need to do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dawn-checking procedure described in steps 12 and 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for setting up such a careful check for daybreak.

steps.title: Moonlight was once mistaken for dawn
steps.stepSummary: Once the moonlight fooled them into thinking it was dawn. They slaughtered the תמיד too early, and it had to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because once the moonlight rose, and they thought the east had lit up. They slaughtered the תמיד, and then had to take it out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question with a story. A real mistake once happened, so they made the check stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering the תמיד before daybreak makes it unfit, and an unfit קרבן is burned. The strict check exists so that this loss does not happen again.

keyTerms.meaning: The light of the moon
The daily communal offering
The place where unfit קדשים are burned

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a תמיד slaughtered at night is unfit. The ברייתא in step 17 builds on this point.

phrases.english: Because once the light of the moon rose,
and they imagined that the east had lit up,
they slaughtered the daily offering,
and they took it out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A past mistake, where moonlight was taken for dawn, caused a תמיד to be slaughtered at night and burned.

steps.title: The כהן גדול immerses, and the Temple rule on purification
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול is taken down to immerse. Anyone who relieves himself in the מקדש needs טבילה, and anyone who urinates needs to wash his hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: They led the כהן גדול down to the place of immersion. This was the rule in the מקדש: anyone who relieves himself needs immersion, and anyone who urinates needs washing of the hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the יום כיפור order: once morning is confirmed, the כהן גדול goes to immerse. It then gives a general Temple rule about when immersion or washing is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of purification. Relieving oneself needs full טבילה. Urinating only needs קידוש ידים ורגלים from the כיור.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of immersion
Literally 'covers his legs', a polite way to say relieving oneself
Requires immersion
Washing of hands and feet from the כיור

phrases.english: And they led the High Priest down to the place of immersion.
This was the principle in the Temple:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַמֵּסֵיךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו טָעוּן טְבִילָה,
phrases.english: anyone who covers his legs requires immersion,
phrases.notes: "Covers his legs" is a polite way of saying he relieved himself.

phrases.english: and anyone who urinates
requires sanctification of hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the יומא משנה after the dawn check.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relieving oneself in the מקדש requires טבילה, and urinating requires קידוש ידים ורגלים.

steps.title: A bird עולה or a מנחה done at night is also burned
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דרבי אבין teaches that a bird עולה pinched at night and a מנחה whose handful was taken at night must also be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רבי אבין teaches: not only this case, but even a bird burnt offering pinched at night, and a meal offering whose handful was taken at night, must go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא widens the rule from the משנה. Like the תמיד slaughtered at night, other offerings whose main service was done at night are burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke only about slaughtering the תמיד. The ברייתא adds מליקה of a bird and קמיצה of a מנחה. When either is done at night, the offering is unfit and burned.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird burnt offering
Was pinched at the neck (מליקה), the way a bird offering is killed
Had its handful removed (קמיצה)

phrases.english: The father of Rabbi Avin teaches:
Not only this case, but
phrases.notes: "This case" is the תמיד slaughtered at night from the story in the משנה.

phrases.english: even a bird burnt offering that was pinched at night,
and a meal offering whose handful was removed at night –
must go out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין לֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the משנה's case of a תמיד slaughtered at night to other offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird עולה pinched at night and a מנחה whose קמיצה was done at night are unfit and burned.

steps.title: Why burn the מנחה if the handful can be put back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the bird case, since a pinched bird cannot be undone. It asks why the מנחה should be burned, when the handful could be returned and taken again by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the bird עולה, because it cannot be undone. But a מנחה: one could return the handful to its place and take it again by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling about the מנחה. No answer is given yet; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird pinched at night is already killed, so nothing can fix it. Flour taken out at night can be mixed back into the מנחה, and a new handful taken in the daytime. So why should the whole מנחה be burned?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for this case), said before a 'but' challenge
To restore it to how it was before
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה
In the daytime

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the bird case. It agrees with that part and challenges only the מנחה.

phrases.english: Granted, a bird burnt offering –
because it is not possible to restore it,
phrases.notes: Once the bird is pinched it is dead, so the act cannot be undone.

phrases.english: but a meal offering –
it is possible that he returns the handful to its place
and removes a handful by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מנחה part of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a מנחה whose קמיצה was done at night must be burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unlike pinching a bird, taking a handful can be undone: the flour can go back into the מנחה and be taken again by day. So burning seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Service vessels make things holy even at the wrong time
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דרבי אבין holds that כלי שרת make their contents holy even when it is not the right time, so a קומץ taken at night cannot be put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is the one who taught this rule, and he is the one who explains it: service vessels make things holy even when it is not their proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18 about why the מנחה must be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 asked why the קומץ could not simply be returned and taken again by day. The answer is that the קומץ was placed in a כלי שרת, and the כלי makes it holy even at night. Once it is holy, it cannot go back to being plain flour, so the problem cannot be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels used for the service in the מקדש
They make something holy
Not at their proper time

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'made holy' here does not mean the offering is good. It means it is now locked into holiness, so if it is ruined, it cannot be undone.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He teaches it, and he says it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is אבוה דרבי אבין from step 17. He taught the ruling and also gives its reason.

phrases.english: Service vessels sanctify even not at their proper time.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 about the מנחה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals the underlying view of the one who taught the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קומץ taken at night could be returned and taken again by day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלי שרת made the קומץ holy even at night, so it cannot be returned and must be burned.

steps.title: A ברייתא about when offerings become holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that links when an offering becomes holy to the time when it is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Anything offered by day becomes holy by day. Anything offered at night becomes holy at night. Anything offered both by day and at night becomes holy both by day and at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the rule from step 19. This step quotes the source, and the next step draws the challenge out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches the time an offering becomes holy to the time it is brought. A מנחה is a daytime offering. That seems to clash with the idea that a כלי can make it holy at night.

keyTerms.meaning: What is offered in the daytime
Becomes holy (here, made holy by the כלי שרת)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Anything offered by day is sanctified by day,
at night – is sanctified at night,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves words out here. Read it as 'anything offered at night is sanctified at night.'

phrases.english: both by day and at night –
is sanctified both by day and at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to contradict step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that כלי שרת מקדשין שלא בזמנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties holiness to the offering's proper time. The full attack comes in the next step.

steps.title: Daytime only, not at night
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'by day' the גמרא learns that a daytime offering does not become holy at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anything offered by day becomes holy by day.' By day, yes; at night, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and finds a direct contradiction to step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a daytime offering becomes holy only 'by day,' then a קומץ put in a כלי at night should not become holy at all. In that case it could be returned and taken again by day, which brings back the question from step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: By day, yes; at night, no (an inference from the exact wording)

phrases.english: Anything offered by day is sanctified by day;
'by day' – yes, 'at night' – no;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'by day' suggests that a daytime offering is not made holy at night. That goes against step 19.

steps.title: Holy enough to be disqualified, not to be offered
steps.stepSummary: At the wrong time the כלי makes the offering holy only enough to become disqualified, not enough to be brought on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not holy enough to be offered, but it is holy enough to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting holiness into two levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means that at night a daytime offering does not get the full holiness needed to be brought on the מזבח. It does get enough holiness to become disqualified. So the night קומץ is stuck: it cannot be offered and cannot be returned, and it must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy enough to be offered
Holy enough to become disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי שרת used at the wrong time makes something 'holy to be disqualified' but not 'holy to be offered.' That is why the night קומץ must be burned.

phrases.english: It is not sanctified to be offered,
but it is sanctified to become disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ לִיקְרַב, אֲבָל קָדוֹשׁ לִיפָּסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a daytime offering gets no holiness at all at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: At night it gets enough holiness to be disqualified, though not enough to be offered.

steps.title: רבי זירא's challenge from the bread placed after שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a משנה: if the bread and frankincense bowls were set on the שולחן after שבת, the fix is to leave them there until the next שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged: If someone set out the bread and the frankincense bowls after שבת and burned the bowls on the next שבת, it is invalid. What should he do? He should leave it until the following שבת. Even if it stays on the Table for many days, nothing is wrong with that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts a new challenge by quoting a משנה. The גמרא is setting up a question, and the answer comes after this step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שולחן is a כלי שרת. Here the bread was placed on it at the wrong time, on a weekday instead of שבת. If כלי שרת make things holy even at the wrong time, we would expect the bread to be locked into holiness and stuck. Yet the משנה simply lets it wait for the next שבת. That seems to show the Table did not make it holy at the wrong time.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranged / set out (the bread on the שולחן)
The bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים
The Table in the מקדש, which is a כלי שרת
How should he act? (what is the fix)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
If he arranged the bread and the bowls
phrases.notes: The bowls hold the frankincense that sits next to the לחם הפנים and is burned when the bread is removed.

phrases.english: after Shabbat,
and burned the bowls on the Shabbat – it is invalid.
phrases.notes: This means the very next שבת, so the bread was on the Table for less than a full week.

phrases.english: How should he act?
He should leave it until the following Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הִיא עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים
phrases.english: for even if it is on the Table many days,
there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the rule of steps 19 and 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bread was placed on the שולחן, a כלי שרת, at the wrong time. Yet the משנה lets it simply wait for the next שבת. This suggests the כלי did not make it holy in a way that ruins it.

steps.title: Why doesn't the bread placed after שבת become holy and then disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains his challenge. If כלי שרת make their contents holy at the wrong time, the bread on the שולחן should become holy and then be ruined by staying overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think כלי שרת make things holy even when it is not their proper time, then the bread placed on the שולחן after שבת should become holy and then become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא spells out why the משנה he quoted is a problem for אבוה דרבי אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דרבי אבין said a כלי makes an offering holy at the wrong time, at least enough to disqualify it. If so, the שולחן should make the bread holy even after שבת, and then staying overnight (לינה) should disqualify it. But the משנה says to just leave it until next שבת, which means the שולחן did not make it holy at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would think (a setup for showing that an idea leads to a problem)
Holy vessels used for the service in the בית המקדש
Not at their proper time
Let it become holy and then become disqualified

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that service vessels make holy
even not at their proper time, (to be disqualified)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, it means holy enough to be ruined.

phrases.english: then let it become holy and be disqualified.
phrases.notes: The bread would become holy on the שולחן and then be ruined by staying overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 23 attacks the answer from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבוה דרבי אבין's view that כלי שרת make an offering holy even at the wrong time, enough to disqualify it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the bread on the שולחן after שבת would become holy and then be disqualified overnight. The משנה says to leave it for next שבת, so it never became holy.

steps.title: The night before counts as the same time, but days early does not
steps.stepSummary: רבה admits the challenge is good. He answers that the night before is not 'too early,' but several days before is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The one raising the challenge raises it well. But אבוה דרבי אבין is also quoting a ברייתא. That תנא holds that night is not considered 'before its time,' but days are considered 'before their time.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה praises רבי זירא's challenge. Then he defends אבוה דרבי אבין, because his view comes from a ברייתא, and explains why the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night before a daytime service belongs to the same unit of time, so a קומץ put in a כלי at night does become holy and is then disqualified. Bread put on the שולחן after שבת is placed several days before its proper time, which is שבת, and that counts as truly 'too early,' so the שולחן does not make it holy at all. This explains why the משנה says to just leave it there until the next שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges well; the objection is a good one
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים from outside the משנה
Lacking time, meaning its proper time has not yet come

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying רבי זירא is wrong. He agrees the question is strong. He only shows that a ברייתא cannot simply be rejected, so we must explain it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule for the sugya: a כלי makes things holy at the 'wrong time' only when it is a little early (the night before), not when it is days early.

phrases.english: רבה said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב – שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב,
phrases.english: The one who raises the objection raises it well,
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי זירא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין נָמֵי מַתְנִיתָא קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: but the father of רבי אבין is also stating a ברייתא.
He holds: night is not considered 'lacking time,'
phrases.notes: The night before a daytime service counts as part of the same day.

phrases.english: but days are considered 'lacking time.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: being a night early is different from being days early.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any 'wrong time' is the same, so the שולחן after שבת should make the bread holy, just like a כלי at night makes a קומץ holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The night before is not considered too early, so the כלי makes it holy. Being several days early is too early, so the שולחן does not make it holy.

steps.title: The גמרא begins another challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'ultimately' to open a new difficulty with רבה's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ultimately,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to push back on רבה's answer, and the challenge itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סוף סוף' signals that even after the distinction just made, some problem still remains. The full challenge is in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, ultimately; opens a point that still stands despite the previous answer

phrases.english: Ultimately,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבה's answer in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's distinction between being a night early and being days early.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Signals that a problem remains even with the distinction. The full argument continues in the next text.
